dimensions.note: The value (content, content_base64 or dotenv entries) reaches the target only over the canonical _lib/ssh.ts stdin upload; private_key goes to a short-lived ssh-agent over stdin and password through an askpass helper, never argv. Every content field, entries values, private_key, password and hmac_key are sensitive-marked. State, logs and method results hold path, mode, owner, group, byte count and flags, plus a keyed HMAC only when hmac_key is supplied; never the value or a plain hash. Live: ps -efww sampled every 50 ms on the control host and the target during writes found 0 hits for values, substrings or their SHA-256 (positive control hit). Known external issue swamp-club lab 3555: README examples use vault references only and never --json. 2026.10.17.2: the value no longer goes through the transport upload temp file; write streams it on exec stdin straight into one remote sh -c script (mktemp beside the destination, cat, length check, chmod, chown -h, no-follow re-check, mv -T). The only value-derived figure in the script text is its byte count, never a content hash (rule 4h); the destination SHA-256 is compared locally. Live on ec4cbd5: ps -efww every 50 ms on control and target across six writes, 22 patterns including substrings and sha256: 0 hits, no 64-hex string on the target, and no .ssh-host-upload* file ever appeared.
Each method logs once with structured placeholders (path, changed, matches, removed); no value, hash, argv or output in log fields.

Every OpenSSH exit 255 maps to a typed SshError (host key, auth, unreachable), live-verified for a wrong pin and an unreachable host with nothing written. A stat failure on an existing file is an error, not not_found; a failed chown or rename removes the stage and writes no state. A symlink or directory destination is refused with a typed SshError before staging and again before the rename (live cell 8 failed on 770114a and passes on 34dd922). 2026.10.17.2: the remote script is POSIX sh (set -eu; the round-1 Critical, set -o pipefail rejected by dash so every changed write failed, is fixed and tested under a real dash). A short stdin (ssh drop or the 120 s local timeout) now fails the staged byte-count check before the rename; HUP/INT/TERM exit 1 and the EXIT trap removes the temp. Live: a kill -9 of the local ssh mid-stream gave exit 137 as a typed failure, the stage was removed and the old file kept (three runs).

56 unit tests (18 model, 38 vendored transport) with an injected runner and a plain-object method context, no process or socket. Live end-to-end: 12/13 on 770114a (cell 8 symlink destination failed), 5/5 on 34dd922 (cells 1, 2, 8, 9, 13). Residual LOW (astra): no test drives the second, pre-rename check with a destination that changes during staging. LOW (astra): the symlink test's fake runner returns the same result on both branches of its condition (dead code). 2026.10.17.2: the canonical transport tests (ssh_test.ts) are vendored; a new test runs the generated write script under a real dash (else sh) for the normal, short-read, symlink and directory cases. Live end-to-end on ec4cbd5: 8/8 (normal write, idempotent re-write, symlink and directory refusal, atomic publish over 2730 samples with 0 missing or partial, killed write, argv and temp scan, remove).

write compares the remote SHA-256, mode and owner/group (names and numeric ids) with the local value and skips the write when all match (live: inode and mtime unchanged); a change stages beside the destination, chowns the stage with chown -h, then mv -T. remove is a clean no-op when absent and removes a dangling symlink. Residual MEDIUM (astra, terra; downgraded under the run rulings): the destination checks and mv -T are separate remote calls, so a symlink planted between them in an attacker-writable parent is replaced (rename does not follow it, so no write-through); a symlinked parent directory is not detected, with the same writable-parent precondition. 2026.10.17.2: the pre-rename symlink/directory re-check now runs inside the same remote script as mv -T, narrowing the check-then-rename window to one shell. Live: an idempotent re-write left inode and mtime unchanged.

Built on the OpenSSH client, ssh-agent/ssh-add with -F /dev/null and IdentityFile=none. write requires GNU mv -T, stat -c and sha256sum on the target and fails closed elsewhere. Dotenv values are single-quoted with ' escaped for POSIX-shell sourcing (live: sh and bash source a hostile value exactly).

Temporary known_hosts, askpass helper and ssh-agent are removed or killed in finally (vendored transport tests). The stage file is removed on any failure (live: no *.secret-stage-* left). Remote output is capped by the transport. 2026.10.17.2: no transport-level temp file; the script's own temp is removed by its EXIT trap on any failure (live: 0 stage files left after all cells). Residual LOW: after a local timeout the remote script runs until its stdin closes, then fails the length check and keeps the old file.

Manifest: @randybias/secret-file 2026.10.17.1 (model version literal matches), two-sentence description, Apache-2.0, additionalFiles README.md and LICENSE.txt. write and remove descriptions start DESTRUCTIVE, verify READ-ONLY. Fixtures use RFC 5737 addresses and synthetic keys; leak scan, gitleaks and fixture guard pass. Merge prep: plain model export so the registry catalogs the type, and the state schema constant renamed so the sensitive-field heuristic no longer matches a non-secret line. 2026.10.17.2: manifest and model version literals 2026.10.17.2; the upgrades entry is one UPGRADES const referenced by createModel and the plain exported model (dry run free of the version-bump warning). Residual LOW: deno.json grants --allow-run=sh,dash to the whole test task. Naming: visibility public, audience general; a rename to ssh-secret-file is proposed and pending Randy.

Global arguments are an empty strictObject; every method argument object is strict. host, user, port, path (absolute, no . or .. components, no trailing slash), mode and owner/group carry grammars. host_key_policy is required and accepts only strict; host_keys is required (1-64). Content is bounded (1 MiB literal, entries 256 keys and 1 MiB rendered). Residual LOW (astra, terra): the rendered-entries cap counts UTF-16 code units, so multibyte values can render to more than 1 MiB of UTF-8.
write (create/update), verify (read) and remove (delete, an action) cover the file's lifecycle on one host.
Path grammar, content-form exclusivity, entries keys and caps, and host-key policy are validated before any spawn; the destination is checked with test -L and test -d before staging.
secret-<32 hex>: SHA-256 over host, port, user and path, truncated to 128 bits, so two files on one host or one path on two hosts get distinct records.
Methods read only this model's own records; every target and value arrives as method arguments, so one generic definition serves any host and path.
